class.name: VegetationField3D
class.brief_description: Places the plants of a [Biome] over a [TerrainDataMap3D].
class.description: Places plants the way Horizon Zero Dawn does (van Muijden, GDC 2017): the map is cut into tiles of [member tile_size]; for each [PlantSpecies] in the [Biome]'s order, a tiled Poisson-disk pattern (Bridson 2007) is laid over each tile and each point is kept when its random rank is below the species' density times its rules there, so density changes smoothly and stays evenly spread. Plants stand on the map's height, keep later species out of their footprint, and are drawn as one [MultiMeshInstance3D] per mesh per tile (internal children, not saved). The result depends only on the map, the biome and [member seed].

method.name: get_placements
method.description: Returns the world positions of the plants of species [param species] (its index in the [Biome]) from the last [method populate].

method.name: get_plant_count
method.description: Number of plants placed by the last [method populate].

method.name: get_populate_time_msec
method.description: Time the last [method populate] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_conifer_at
method.description: Share of the canopy over [param global_position] that is needle-leaved ([member PlantSpecies.canopy_conifer]), weighted by how much each crown covers it: [code]0.0[/code] under broadleaf trees or in the open, [code]1.0[/code] under conifers.

method.name: get_floor_shader_code
method.description: Shader code for terrain materials: [code]forest_floor(world_pos, albedo)[/code] returns the ground's albedo with the forest floor laid over it where the canopy closes, leaf litter under broadleaf crowns, needles over duff with feather moss drifts under conifers, a patchwork in mixed stands. It reads the [code]forest_floor_map[/code] and [code]forest_floor_rect[/code] global shader parameters (see [member forest_floor_enabled]). Use it in a fragment shader. [method GrassField3D.get_ground_shader_code] includes it and its [code]grass_ground()[/code] calls it, so materials that use the grass ground get the litter too. It also gives [code]vegetation_far(world_pos, albedo, camera_pos)[/code]: call it after [code]grass_ground()[/code] with [code]CAMERA_POSITION_WORLD[/code]. Where plants with a [member PlantSpecies.far_color] grew, it blends their colour into the ground as the plant shader thins them away with distance, with the same curve: none up to 35% of the species' range, all of it at the range. It reads the [code]vegetation_far_map[/code], [code]vegetation_far_rect[/code] and [code]vegetation_far_range[/code] global shader parameters, published after each [method populate] that places such plants.

method.name: get_shade_at
method.description: Canopy shade at [param global_position], from 0 (open sky) to 1 (dense crown), from the plants of species with [member PlantSpecies.canopy_radius] placed by the last [method populate]. Each crown stops [member PlantSpecies.canopy_opacity] of the light under its core, fading out a little past its rim; overlapping crowns multiply their transmission. Species with a [member PlantSpecies.shade_range] are placed by it, so list canopy species first in the [Biome].

method.name: populate
method.description: Places every species over the whole data map, replacing earlier plants. Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] without a [member biome] or a baked map.

method.name: queue_populate
method.description: Populates at the end of the frame, once.

members.member: A density mask over [member density_mask_rect], read once per [method populate] (bilinear). Each species with a [member PlantSpecies.mask_channel] multiplies its suitability by that channel (or by one minus it with [member PlantSpecies.mask_invert]), the way open-world tools paint or generate per-layer density maps (Unreal's landscape layer weights for grass types, Unity's terrain detail maps, Horizon Zero Dawn's density maps per ecotope). Paint a clearing as 0 in the trees' channel and the meadow's species can read the same channel inverted. Outside the rect the mask counts as 1.
The world rectangle (x and z, metres) that [member density_mask] covers.
The [TerrainDataMap3D] that gives height, slope, wetness and water. Its area is the area planted.
If [code]true[/code], populate when ready (once the map is baked) and again whenever the map is baked again, after terrain edits.
Seed of the point patterns. The same seed gives the same plants.
Width in metres of a tile: one point pattern and one [MultiMeshInstance3D] per mesh per tile, so tiles out of view are culled.

If [code]true[/code], each [method populate] that places canopy crowns publishes canopy closure ([method get_shade_at]) and conifer share ([method get_conifer_at]) on half-metre cells over the data map's rect as the [code]forest_floor_map[/code] and [code]forest_floor_rect[/code] global shader parameters, read by [method get_floor_shader_code]. A field without crowns leaves them as they are, so one field can own the trees while others place the plants.

Path to a [WeatherMap3D]. After each [method populate] the placed canopy species are written to its [member WeatherMap3D.canopy_map] over the data map's rect (about 1 m cells): crown top height in red, leaf area index over 4 in green, taking [member PlantSpecies.canopy_opacity] as [code]1 - exp(-0.5 LAI)[/code]. [method WeatherMap3D.get_canopy_closure_at] then matches [method get_shade_at], and snow, wind and light under the trees all see the same forest. This replaces any canopy map already set there.
